message: Could I get a refill on my losartan? I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years, my blood pressure is well controlled, last home reading was 122/78.

findings.finding: Losartan 50 mg once daily for approximately 2 years
findings.quote: I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years
my blood pressure is well controlled

findings.finding: Recent home blood pressure reading 122/78 mmHg

basis.quote: I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years, my blood pressure is well controlled
basis.interpretation: Stable chronic hypertension on established dose with reported good control
Recent home blood pressure measurement within normal range, consistent with reported control

output.reason: Routine medication refill for stable, long-standing hypertension with demonstrated control; clinician review needed to confirm continued appropriateness and authorize refill.

Routine refill request for long-standing losartan 50 mg daily with a reported well-controlled home reading of 122/78 and no reported new symptoms, so a clinician prescribing review can proceed asynchronously.
output.patientMessage: I've asked our Counsel clinical team to review your losartan refill in this thread; your reported home reading of 122/78 and two years on a stable dose suggest routine continuation. Keep taking it as prescribed and keep logging home readings. If you run out before the refill arrives, contact your pharmacy. Seek urgent care for fainting, chest pain, severe headache, or new weakness or speech trouble.
differential: Stable treated essential hypertension needing prescription continuation
Medication supply gap without clinical change

redFlags.concern: Medication side effects or adherence problems
Currently out of medication / lapse in supply

output.vitalSigns: Patient reports a home blood pressure of 122/78 ("last home reading was 122/78"); timing, device and technique not reported, and heart rate and other vitals not reported.
output.evidenceLimitations: Only a single self-reported home reading is available, with no reported recent labs, adherence details or side-effect history.

citations.quote: Your blood pressure is considered high when you have consistent systolic readings of 130 mm Hg or higher or diastolic readings of 80 mm Hg or higher.
citations.claim: A reading of 122/78 falls below the high blood pressure threshold, consistent with the patient's report of good control.
citations.limitation: Patient education categories rely on consistent readings; one home value does not confirm ongoing control.
